title: Cleanest space to track and reflect
body: I rarely make $ contributions but jumped at the chance to ‘tip’ the developers. I’ve tried many different tracking and journaling apps but I feel Way of Life is the perfect balance between a. putting things down, and b. being able to review later. Firstly, it’s not fidgety to mark yes or to write a journal entry which means I can be consistent. Secondly, the multi month view gives me such a quick look at my progress. Way of Life also has the BEST excel export I’ve tried if I want to nerd out. Would be fantastic, if there was a way to ‘Star’ really important journal entries (because as someone who journals everyday I want to easily find my A Ha / breakthrough moments). Highly recommend!

title: Excellent!
body:
I've tried loads of habit-changing/to-do apps and this is so far the best one. 
I love that you can go back a few days and add what you did, even if you forgot to do it on the actual day - which means you don't lose your progress and you get a better analysis. 
Adding notes to things is also another great feature, because you can explain why you failed to achieve it that day. 
Many of these apps leave you feeling like you have failed because you missed a day or two, which not only results in no longer wanting to use it, but also diminishes the likelihood that you will keep up the good habits you're trying to achieve. 

The design is fairly basic but I don't think that is a bad thing, it is easy to read and learn to use which again, is another plus compared to other, unnecessarily complex, apps.

I would love to see a few more things in there like perhaps the ability to add goals and goal dates and rewards and so on to condition the habits and keep track of successes.

Great app!

title: Good, but could be great
body:
Great idea - and sweet app! I can see myself using this every day and suggesting it to a LOT of people.
However, I'd like to give feedback that could move the product forward.

1
Scrolling tap.
In journal, the current green/red/skip entry mechanic feels clunky. How about tap once on a day for green, tap twice for red, tap three times for skip? Or hold finger on the day and the three colours pop up in a menu (same UX as if you hold your finger on an iOS keyboard character?)

2
Set default skip days when creating new habit.
ie, when creating a new habit the user is presented with a week view template on which they can choose their default, recurring 'skip' days. If I'm doing yoga twice a week it's annoying to have to continually, manually enter 'skip' for the other five days, it'd be nice if I set those skips days on a template when I first created the habit so I didn't have to keep re-entering them.

3
Upcoming habits.
It'd be fun to create future habits that sit inactive, perhaps below in the journal. I can set a date they go live, or activate them when I'm ready. This also serves to keep the user engaged with the app.

Thanks and good luck!
